items.title: Peasy runs at national scale: more than 150 experts, 70 offices, more than 50,000 contracts a year and more than 50 partners
items.summary: The Peasy 'over ons' page states '>150 experten, 70 winkels, >50.000 contracten afgesloten per jaar, >50 partners' and a customer satisfaction of 4.5/5. Peasy is headquartered in Zaventem, runs customer care from Hasselt and Oujda (Morocco), serves customers in Dutch and French, and presents itself as 'onderdeel van een familie van merken' (peasy.be, hypotheekwinkel.be, verzekeringen.be, aanbieders.be).
items.implication: Implication for the domain: the platform must serve three distinct volumes at once — a comparison flow that concludes tens of thousands of insurance, energy and telecom contracts per year, a mortgage flow that runs through 70 offices, and a partner flow that reconciles fees from more than 50 counterparties — so throughput per advisor and per partner feed are first-order design constraints, not reporting afterthoughts.

items.title: The consumer pays nothing extra: partners pay a referral fee when a contract is concluded through Peasy, and Peasy is never the contracting party
items.summary: The Peasy customer-service FAQ explains that partners pay an 'aanbrengvergoeding' (referral fee) when a contract is concluded via Peasy, that the consumer pays nothing extra, and that customers never contract with Peasy itself — the contract is always concluded with the partner. hypotheek.winkel's 'gratis, hoe kan dat?' page states that its advice is free for the buyer because the commission comes from the bank's head office, and the site quotes: 'of je nu rechtstreeks naar hen stapt of via ons, jij betaalt geen (pro)cent meer'.
items.implication: Implication for the domain: revenue is recognised per concluded contract, not per advice hour, so the platform must trace every lead to a partner-confirmed conclusion (loan disbursed, policy bound, switch executed) and reconcile that against partner commission statements; independence must be demonstrable in the advice record because the payer is the partner, not the household.

items.title: hypotheek.winkel has compared the daily conditions of 25 banks since 2001 and is rated 4.8/5 on Trustpilot
items.summary: hypotheekwinkel.be (hypotheek.winkel BV, BE 0474.087.795, Zaventem) states that the chain started in 2001, operates '70 hypotheek.winkels' across Flanders and Brussels, compares the conditions of 25 banks daily and is free for the buyer. The 'klanten vertellen' page shows a Trustpilot score of 4.8/5.
items.implication: Implication for the domain: the same-screen comparison of 25 banks is the core workbench capability and depends on a daily bank rate and conditions feed; the Trustpilot score is a public conversion asset, so review capture after the notary deed and review display on office pages belong in the engagement flow rather than being left to marketing.

items.title: The feasibility certificate turns a 25-bank comparison of salary and savings into proof a buyer can show a seller
items.summary: The haalbaarheidscertificaat page describes a feasibility certificate that compares 25 banks on the buyer's salary and savings and takes into account the renovation obligation for homes with a low EPC label; buyers show the certificate to sellers as proof of their borrowing capacity.
items.implication: Implication for the domain: the certificate is the first product a first-time buyer receives, before any loan exists, so its issuance rate and turnaround are leading indicators for the whole mortgage funnel; the EPC renovation obligation must be encoded as a rule in the feasibility calculation and reused unchanged in the later credit file.

items.title: Seven mortgage simulators and seven project types define the digital front door of the mortgage brokerage
items.summary: hypotheekwinkel.be offers simulators for 'hoeveel kan ik lenen', 'maandlast', 'rentevoet', 'financieel plan', 'notariskosten', 'haalbaarheid' and 'aflossingstabel', and organises its advice by project: first home, next home, second home, new build, refinancing, buying as a self-employed person and renovation loan.
items.implication: Implication for the domain: simulators are the demand engine for the office network, so every simulator result should be capturable as a lead with the project type attached and routed to the nearest office with the expert prepared; project types should be first-class attributes of the lead, the appointment and the credit file rather than free text.

items.title: Upload-your-proposal, callback requests and office or video-call appointments convert online interest into an expert conversation
items.summary: peasy.be offers 'upload je voorstel', a free expert review of a mortgage or insurance proposal received elsewhere, callback requests, and appointment booking in an office or by video call; the home page promises 'besparen zonder gedoe' across mortgage loans, insurance and energy under one roof.
items.implication: Implication for the domain: the proposal-review intake is the cheapest way to win refinancing and switch cases because the household has already done the shopping, so review turnaround should be measured in hours and the uploaded proposal should pre-fill the comparison rather than being retyped by the expert.

items.title: The budget barometer benchmarks a household's fixed costs against Belgian averages before any comparison starts
items.summary: The peasy.be budgetbarometer page lets a household compare its fixed costs with Belgian averages to see where it overpays.
items.implication: Implication for the domain: the barometer is a diagnostic that ranks which contract to compare first, so each barometer category should map directly to a comparison module (insurance, energy, telecom, mortgage) and the identified overpayment should become the target figure the customer-care advisor and the monitoring alerts report against.

items.title: Peasy keeps watching the contracts it brokered and warns the household when a better or cheaper option exists
items.summary: The customer-service FAQ states that Peasy monitors the contracts concluded through it and warns customers when a better or cheaper option is available; the home page positions mortgage loans, insurance and energy under one roof.
items.implication: Implication for the domain: a monitored contract vault per household is the product that turns a one-off mortgage into a multi-contract relationship; the monitoring rules need partner tariff feeds that are current enough to justify an alert, and alert acceptance rate is the measure of whether the promise is kept without annoying the household.

items.title: Aanbieders.be advertises concrete savings per contract type, free switching and a 4.6 Google rating from 2,765 reviews
items.summary: aanbieders.be shows '4,6 / 2765 Google reviews' and advertises savings of up to €600 on energy on its homepage (and 'tot 1.100€ deze winter' on its energy page), €500 on insurance compared across 11 insurers, €348 on internet/TV/telephony and €144 on mobile; switching is free, it also covers charging stations and business energy and telecom, and it is open Monday to Thursday until 17:00 and Friday until 16:00.
items.implication: Implication for the domain: the savings claims are the conversion promise and must be backed by the comparison engine's actual savings distribution per category; since the advisors work office hours, the self-service comparison and callback queue must absorb evening and weekend demand and hand a ready quote to the advisor the next morning.

items.title: Verzekeringen.be spans eighteen insurance lines and names the insurers it compares, from AXA and Allianz to DELA and Qover
items.summary: verzekeringen.be (Assurances.be in French; acquired by the group in 2021) covers car, motor, bike, travel, cancellation, luggage, fire, contents, outstanding-balance, hospitalisation, accident, dental, family liability, pension savings, funeral, pet, legal assistance and self-employed cover, with insurer pages for AXA, Allianz, Ethias, KBC, Belfius, DVV, DKV, DELA, NN, Athora, Cardif, Euromex, Europ Assistance, Fidea, Patronale Life, Qover, Santevet and DAS.
items.implication: Implication for the domain: the insurance comparison module must model very different products (a funeral policy and an outstanding-balance policy share little beyond a premium) and different binding paths per insurer, so product-line templates and per-insurer quote and bind integrations are the scaling constraint; outstanding-balance and fire cover are the natural bridge from the mortgage file to the insurance brands.

items.title: Customer care for insurance, energy and telecom runs from Hasselt and Oujda in Dutch and French
items.summary: Peasy states that its customer care operates from Hasselt and from Oujda in Morocco, serves customers in Dutch and French, and publishes the contact number 03 501 22 22.
items.implication: Implication for the domain: advisors in two countries handle contacts arriving under three brand names, so the care desk needs one omnichannel inbox with brand and language context, shared scripts and a knowledge base, and the customer-account data must be accessible under GDPR from Oujda with the same consent and audit controls as in Hasselt.

items.title: Vortex built Peasy in five years from a 68-branch mortgage chain into a three-brand comparison group and kept investing through a 40 percent market contraction
items.summary: Vortex Capital Partners invested in Hypotheek.winkel in 2020, when it had 68 physical branches and proprietary comparison technology, and formed Horizon Group with management the same year; the group acquired Verzekeringen.be/Assurances.be in 2021 and Aanbieders.be/Mesfournisseurs.be in 2022. Vortex states that it kept investing while the Belgian mortgage market contracted by about 40 percent, and lists the investment as realised with the December 2025 exit to Meilleurtaux; David Geerts is quoted: 'Vortex played a crucial role in every key phase of this journey'.
items.implication: Implication for the domain: diversification into insurance, energy and telecom is the hedge against mortgage cyclicality, so the household relationship must be measured across all contract types and the office network's economics cannot depend on mortgage volume alone; the proprietary comparison technology is the asset the acquirer paid for and should stay a product, not a per-office spreadsheet.

items.title: An in-house academy trains about 30 advisors a year because the market cannot supply mortgage experts
items.summary: Vortex describes an in-house training academy that educates about 30 advisors annually.
items.implication: Implication for the domain (combined with the domain brief's assumption that the mortgage expert is a scarce-skill role, knelpuntberoep, largely trained in-house): advisor supply is a planned capacity, so the academy needs enrolment, curriculum, certification and FSMA-knowledge evidence as product features, and office growth plans should be capacity-checked against certified experts rather than against lead volume alone; expert retention protects a scarce investment of roughly a year's cohort per 30 hires.

items.title: The office network moved from 68 branches in 2020 to 63 locations with 83 experts in January 2024 and 70 offices with more than 150 experts today
items.summary: Vortex reports 68 physical branches at the 2020 investment; franchise.be reported on 22 January 2024 that hypotheek.winkel had 63 locations and 83 experts and had been through a management buy-in backed by private equity since 2020; Peasy's 'over ons' page now states 70 offices and more than 150 experts.
items.implication: Implication for the domain: the number of offices has been broadly stable while the expert count per office has grown, so the franchise model's value is in experts per office and appointments per expert rather than in opening locations; production and conversion dashboards should be per expert and per office, and academy output should be tied to office capacity plans.

items.title: Meilleurtaux acquires 100 percent of Peasy, creating an 81-office national platform led from Belgium by David Geerts
items.summary: On 23 December 2025 hypotheek.winkel announced that Meilleurtaux agreed to acquire 100 percent of the shares of Peasy, which has about 200 employees, revenues of around €30 million and about 70 offices. Meilleurtaux was founded in 1999, has had Silver Lake as majority shareholder since 2020, entered Belgium in 2023 through the acquisition of MiD Finance and is active mainly in Wallonia with offices in Ghent and Antwerp; the combined group has 81 offices, David Geerts leads the Belgian and Luxembourg operations, Thomas Vandeville is CEO of Meilleurtaux, and VDP acted as exclusive advisor to Peasy and Vortex.
items.implication: Implication for the domain: the year-one agenda is integration — one lead engine feeding 81 bilingual offices, shared bank and insurer relationships, and consumer credit and credit grouping (a Meilleurtaux strength) added to the offer — so brand routing, language routing and partner catalogues must be built as configuration rather than hard-coded per brand.

items.title: Belgian mortgage demand fell by roughly a third in 2023 and started recovering in 2024, making broker volume highly cyclical
items.summary: Febelfin reported that mortgage credit applications excluding refinancing were down about 37 percent in Q1 2023 and about 29 percent in Q2 2023 compared with 2022, and up about 7.5 percent in number and about 12 percent in amount in Q3 2024.
items.implication: Implication for the domain: lead volume and expert utilisation can swing by a third within a year, so the office network needs conversion and file-throughput metrics that hold in a downturn, refinancing and insurance cross-sell to fill capacity when purchase demand drops, and forecasting inputs for banks that plan broker-channel volume.

items.title: Credit and insurance intermediaries must be registered with the FSMA, and hypotheek.winkel names the FPS Economy Economic Inspectorate as its supervisor
items.summary: The FSMA keeps registers of credit intermediaries in mortgage credit and consumer credit and of insurance intermediaries; hypotheekwinkel.be names the FPS Economy Economic Inspectorate as its supervisory authority.
items.implication: Implication for the domain: every expert and customer-care advisor who advises on credit or insurance must be traceable to a valid registration, the academy's certification evidence must satisfy FSMA knowledge requirements, and advice and suitability records must be retained per file so that an inspection can be answered from the system across all three brands.

items.title: BIPT Easy Switch lets the new fixed operator terminate the old contract, with more than 99,125 switches in 2021
items.summary: Under BIPT's Easy Switch procedure the new fixed telecom operator terminates the customer's old contract; BIPT reported more than 99,125 Easy Switch switches in 2021.
items.implication: Implication for the domain: telecom switching can be executed end-to-end by the advisor without the household contacting the old operator, so the switch-execution flow should capture the Easy Switch identifiers up front and treat termination as part of the same order; the same 'we cancel the old contract' promise should be reproduced for insurance and energy where the procedures differ.

items.title: Public comparison tools — the VREG V-test and V-check and the FSMA's Wikifin — set the free baseline Peasy must beat with service
items.summary: The VREG V-test and V-check compare energy contracts in Flanders; the V-check reads an invoice code that has been mandatory since 1 July 2025, and VRT reported tens of thousands of uses in the first two months. Wikifin is the FSMA's financial-education programme launched on 31 January 2013 with a savings-account comparison tool and an IMMOsimulator.
items.implication: Implication for the domain: households can already compare energy contracts and simulate a home purchase for free with public tools, so Peasy's differentiation is execution (the switch, the file, the cancellation) and monitoring rather than the comparison itself; the energy module should accept the same invoice-code inputs so that a V-check user can be converted to a switch in one step.

items.title: Immotheker Finotheker competes with 100 offices, 16 banks compared daily, more than 55,000 loans concluded and a mortgage monitor since 2004
items.summary: Immotheker Finotheker presents itself as '100% independent' with '+10,000 products compared', '100 offices', '+55,000 loans concluded', '150 employees' and '30 years experience'; it compares more than 2,000 mortgage loans at 16 banks daily, opened its first office on 1 April 1995 in Schoten, has run a mortgage monitor since 2004 and introduced an attestation of purchase security in 2024.
items.implication: Implication for the domain: the closest competitor already offers the two features Peasy relies on — a feasibility attestation for sellers and a mortgage monitor — and a larger office footprint, so Peasy's edge must come from 25 versus 16 banks, the multi-contract household relationship and the combined 81-office bilingual network; feature parity on certificate and monitor is table stakes.
